Requested from you:

Hi all — quick set of recommendations based on Acme's stated goals and volume: 

1) Recommended model families (initial eval):
- Redwood-median-13B (quantized FP16/INT8) — good balance of cost and factuality for KB-driven replies.
- Redwood-extended-70B (FP16) — for comparison on complex, ambiguous tickets where nuance matters.
- OpenFamily-Stream-Lite — low-cost fallback for peak traffic.

2) Benchmarking assets:
- I've uploaded a short benchmarking report we ran on a similar KB-driven use-case (see link): benchmarking_report_acme_q2.pdf
- Metrics to track in pilot: top-1 accuracy, suggested-reply accept rate, hallucination rate, latency p50/p95.

3) Prompt engineering notes / redaction guidance:
- Keep user-visible outputs free of raw PII. Replace with placeholders and rehydrate client-side when possible.
- Strip any long-form logs from requests — only include ticket summary + relevant KB excerpts.
- We'll provide a redaction script (attached redaction_guidelines.md) and a small example pipeline for client-side masking.

4) Pilot plan: 2-week offline eval (1000 tickets), then 4-week live A/B with gradual ramp. We can provide cost estimates once you confirm model family preference.

If helpful, I can schedule a short technical sync next week to walk through the benchmark and the prompt set template.

Regards,
Rishi
